meta.purpose: Estimate the regular-ticket value of each logged trip for the KlimaTicket break-even ("hat sich das Ticket rentiert?") calculation.
meta.oebb_price_basis: ÖBB Standardticket (Vollpreis, no discount), 2nd class, sales channel Online/Mobile (shop.oebbtickets.at / ÖBB App), bought on the day of travel = column "ST VP 000" in the official ÖBB Relationspreise tables valid from 14.12.2025.

next_oebb_price_change.note: ÖBB: Standardtickets and Vorteilscard +3.5% on average from 13.12.2026; Sparschiene from-prices unchanged. Check: Wien-Innsbruck 1st class online 14-1 days ahead 178.20 -> 184.44 (= x1.035 exactly; 178.20 is the ST VP 014-001 value in the table).
validation_of_parsed_table: Wien-St. Veit/Glan 2nd online day-of: table 62.30 == press "bisher 62,30" (new 64.50); 15+ days: 58.60*1.035=60.65 ~ press 60.70
Linz-Kufstein 2nd Vorteilscard online day-of: table 31.90 == press "bisher 31,90" (new 33.00)

raw_data_files: oebb_relation_prices_major.json (exact official ÖBB prices: 33 major origins x all destinations = 29,883 relations, 2nd+1st class online day-of-travel, plus OSM coordinates for 818 station names)
examples.json (43 named relations with all channels, OSM rail km, haversine, detour)
pairs_all.json (210,807 origin-destination pairs with official price, OSM rail km, haversine km; fit input)
meta.method: Parsed 10 of the 37 official ÖBB Relationspreise PDFs (origins starting BJ-BZ, GOM-GZ, I, KA-KL, LA-LE, LF-LZ, SA-SC, SQ-ST, STA-SZ, WF-WZ). For each origin->destination the cheapest route variant was taken. Rail km = shortest path on the OpenStreetMap railway network (railway=rail|narrow_gauge, sidings/yards excluded) between OSM station nodes, plus one virtual edge Kufstein<->Salzburg Hbf (122.4 km) for the German "DB Korridor" (Rosenheim-Kufstein Grenze 31.868 km + Rosenheim-Salzburg Hbf 88.551 km per Wikipedia + ~2 km estimate). Intra-city pairs (e.g. Wien X -> Wien Y, flat 2.40) excluded from the fit. Robust (soft-L1) least squares on relative error.

oebb_standard_ticket.tariff_table_note: ÖBB does not publish a EUR-per-km formula (the Handbuch für Reisen mit den ÖBB in Österreich, valid from 15.10.2026, only says prices are shown in the sales systems). Instead ÖBB publishes per-relation price tables (Relationspreise) for every station pair, all channels, 1st/2nd class, Vorteilscard, week/month passes. Prices are symmetric (A->B == B->A, verified on 12,175 pairs).

model_price_vs_rail_km.formula: price = clamp(interp(rail_km, knots_km, values_eur), 2.40, 101.20); round to 0.10
model_price_vs_rail_km.note: Minimum fare 2.40 EUR and maximum (cap) 101.20 EUR (2nd class, online, day of travel) are taken directly from the tables (min/max observed; 9,079 relations sit exactly at 101.20). Effective rate ~0.22-0.24 EUR/km up to ~250 km, degressive beyond, cap reached at ~650-730 km (Wien-Bregenz, 697 km, is at the cap).

model_simple_two_segment.formula: price = clamp(a + b*km for km<=k1; a + b*k1 + b2*(km-k1) for km>k1, 2.40, 101.20)

model_price_vs_haversine_km.note: Calibrated on ALL station pairs (dominated by branch-line pairs with large detours) -> overestimates typical main-line trips; prefer haversine x detour_factor -> rail model for main-line trips.

optional_adjustments.note: Residual analysis: trips to/from the tariff point "Innsbruck" cost ~+1.7 EUR more than the km model (tight IQR), "Linz" ~+0.9 EUR; others inconsistent. Routes through the German "DB Korridor" (Kufstein-Rosenheim-Salzburg, e.g. Innsbruck-Salzburg, Tirol/Vorarlberg-Linz/Wien) cost ~+9-10 EUR more than the km model below ~300 km (ratio 1.27 at 100-200 km, 1.18 at 200-300 km, shrinking towards the 101.20 cap). Apply only when no exact relation price is available.

channel_vs_online.im Zug_short_trips_note: on board adds ~14.40 EUR fixed for short trips (<15 EUR)

multipliers.note: Medians over ~95,000 relations (files I, LF-LZ, BJ-BZ); extremely tight distributions (1st/2nd 1.951-1.958 across all price bands).

vorteilscard.note: Classic is for everyone (the former Vorteilscard 66 was merged into Classic in 2025). Comfort adds 50% on seat reservations. Vorteilscard prices also rise ~3.5% on 13.12.2026 (new amounts not yet published).

klimaticket_oe_reference.note: As listed in the VMOBIL tariff table "Stand 01.06.2026" (secondary listing; verify against klimaticket.at).

detour_factor_recommended.evidence: Named example relations (43, typical city-to-city / along-line trips): median rail/haversine 1.20 (p25 1.12, p75 1.35; <50 km 1.15, >=50 km 1.26). Pairs among ~60 major stations (1,825): median 1.47 (2-25 km 1.15, 25-50 km 1.35, 50-350 km ~1.50, >350 km 1.43). All 210k station pairs: median 1.54 (branch-to-branch detours).

recommended_estimation_pipeline: 1. Exact lookup: if both stations are known and the pair is in oebb_relation_prices_major.json (29,883 official relations from 33 major origins incl. Wien, Innsbruck, Salzburg, Linz, Graz, Klagenfurt, St. Pölten, Landeck-Zams, St. Anton am Arlberg, Bludenz, Bregenz), use p2 (2nd) / p1 (1st). Prices are symmetric, so also look up B->A.

2. If the rail distance is known (journey planner leg distance or bundled rail graph): price = clamp(interp(rail_km, knots, values), 2.40, 101.20). Optional: +1.70 EUR if one end is the tariff point Innsbruck, +9.50 EUR (then cap 101.20) if the route uses the DB-Korridor via Kufstein-Rosenheim-Salzburg.
3. Otherwise: rail_km = haversine_km x detour (1.20 for an obvious along-the-line trip, else banded 1.15/1.30/1.45) and apply step 2.
4. Apply multipliers: 1st class x1.951; Vorteilscard x0.5; reference channel Online/Mobile day-of-travel (Automat x1.086, counter x1.236); from 13.12.2026 multiply by 1.035 and round to 0.10 EUR.
5. Local city trips: use city_and_regional_tickets.recommended_defaults_eur (e.g. Wien 3.20, Innsbruck 3.30).
6. Show the result as an estimate ("ca."), and let the user override the value per trip.

city_and_regional_tickets.note: Single-ride / day tickets for the city core zones. Use as default value for a logged local trip (tram, bus, U-Bahn, S-Bahn inside a city). The ÖBB tables price intra-Wien rail trips at a flat 2.40 EUR (ÖBB-own city fare), but the fare actually paid by most riders is the Wiener Linien/VOR Kernzone ticket.

Wien.notes: 48h/72h tickets discontinued 1.1.2026. Previous single price 2.40. Tariffs will be indexed to CPI from 2027 (details expected autumn 2026; CPI Aug25-Aug26 +3.2%).
Wien.source_note: Official Wiener Linien factsheet "Neue Tarifstruktur" (09.2025), hosted by Österreichischer Behindertenrat; wienerlinien.at itself was bot-protected.

Innsbruck.notes: Printed single valid 45 min, online 90 min. Validity date not stated on the page (retrieved 2026-10-09).

Tirol_regional_VVT.notes: Zone-based regional tariff; exact zone count per trip not modelled. For rail trips inside Tirol use the ÖBB relation price instead.

Vorarlberg_VMOBIL.notes: New zone system LOKAL/REGIO/MAXIMO since 1.6.2026 (no separate city tariff; LOKAL = home municipality + neighbours).

Salzburg.notes: Price for ticket machine / smartphone / online; 60 min unlimited transfers.

Linz.notes: MINI = boarding stop + max. 4 following stops. Outside the Kernzone the OÖVV regional tariff applies (not researched).

Steiermark_regional_Verbund_Linie.superseded_note: Verbund Linie raised tariffs ~3.5% on 1.7.2026 (Graz 1-zone 3.20 -> 3.30); the zone table below is the 1.5.2026 version, multiply by ~1.035 for current values (estimate).

Klagenfurt.notes: Price columns are unlabelled image alt-texts on the page; mapping 2.60 = bought on bus, 2.30 = app/prepaid card is an inference (KMG says app/prepaid stay cheaper). No validity date on page; Kärntner Linien raised regional tariffs ~2.76% on 1.7.2026.

VVNB.status: Verkehrsverbund Niederösterreich-Burgenland no longer exists as a separate tariff: management merged into VOR (2002), tariff systems unified in 2016. Use VOR tariffs for Lower Austria/Burgenland.

recommended_defaults_eur.note: Full-fare standard (non-app) single ticket of the core zone. fallback_other_towns = ÖBB minimum fare 2.40 EUR (official minimum in the Relationspreise tables), used where no city tariff was verified (e.g. Villach, St. Pölten, Wels, Steyr city buses were NOT verified).

full_cost_per_km.assumptions: Ayvens Car Cost Index 2026: TCO over first 4 years at 30,000 km/year (depreciation, maintenance, tyres, energy, taxes, comprehensive insurance); per-km values = monthly cost / 2,500 km. At typical private mileage (10-15k km/year) per-km cost is substantially higher.
full_cost_per_km.oeamtc_note: No current (2026) ÖAMTC headline EUR/km figure found; ÖAMTC offers a per-model calculator (oeamtc.at Auto-Info). Older ÖAMTC example: 0.62 EUR/km at 12,000 km/yr, 0.40 EUR/km at 24,000 km/yr (~2023, outdated).

car_comparison.recommended_note: Use the official Kilometergeld (0.50 EUR/km) as the car-cost comparison; it is close to real full costs of a mid-size car and is the number Austrians know.

tram_and_ubahn.note: UBA list has no tram/U-Bahn line. Proxy: UBA electric rail value (direct+upstream). Wiener Linien state traction power for trams/U-Bahn/e-buses is 100% renewable.

recommended_app_values_direct_plus_upstr.note: Well-to-wheel (direct + fuel/electricity supply), excluding vehicle production. Saved CO2 per trip = (174.0 - mode_value) * km. UBA warns values are not comparable with its earlier lists (method change).
